expectedText:
SPOUSAL OR DOMESTIC PARTNER PROPERTY PETITION — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Pat Morgan · March 15, 2026

SPOUSAL OR DOMESTIC PARTNER PROPERTY PETITION — INFORMATION AND BACKGROUND
This information sheet discusses the California superior court petition procedure of Probate Code §§ 13650-13660, sometimes called a spousal or domestic partner property petition, in connection with the estate of Pat Morgan, who died on March 15, 2026. Taylor Morgan is the surviving spouse or registered domestic partner of Pat Morgan. The property discussed is: Checking account #1234 at Acme Bank; 2019 furniture and household items located at 123 Main St. Under this procedure, a petition may be filed in the superior court for Sacramento County, California, requesting an order that administration of some or all of Pat Morgan's estate is unnecessary because the property described passes to Taylor Morgan, and/or an order confirming that property already belongs to Taylor Morgan under Probate Code §§ 100 or 101. This document is background information only. It is not the petition itself, is not filed with any court, and does not by itself request, obtain, or constitute any court order. Only a petition actually filed with the superior court, followed by notice, and a hearing resulting in a signed court order, can determine that administration is unnecessary or confirm ownership of any property.

TWO DISTINCT REQUESTS THE STATUTE ALLOWS IN ONE PETITION
Probate Code § 13650(a) authorizes a petition to request either or both of two distinct things: first, an order that administration of all or part of the deceased spouse's estate is not necessary because that property is 'property passing to the surviving spouse' (for example, by intestate succession or by the decedent's will); and second, an order confirming the ownership of property that already belongs to the surviving spouse under § 100 (the surviving spouse's own one-half of the community property) or § 101 (the surviving spouse's own one-half of the quasi-community property) — property that was never the decedent's to begin with. Probate Code § 13656 confirms the statute treats these as separate determinations: subdivision (a) directs the court, when it finds the estate is property passing to the surviving spouse, to issue an order 'determining that the property is property passing to the surviving spouse, and determining that no administration is necessary,' while subdivision (c) separately directs the court, on the confirmation branch, to issue an order 'confirming the ownership of the surviving spouse' where the petition described the survivor's own § 100 or § 101 interest and the court so finds. Subdivision (b) further allows a mixed outcome, with the court finding that part of the estate is not property passing to the surviving spouse (and is therefore subject to administration) while the remaining part is.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-03]
  "A surviving spouse or the personal representative, guardian of the estate, or conservator of the estate of the surviving spouse may file a petition in the superior court of the county in which the estate of the deceased spouse may be administered requesting an order that administration of all or part of the estate is not necessary for the reason that all or part of the estate is property passing to the surviving spouse. The petition may also request an order confirming the ownership of the surviving spouse of property belonging to the surviving spouse under Section 100 or 101."
  — Cal. Prob. Code § 13650(a), California Probate Code, the two requests a spousal or domestic partner property petition may make (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=13650.)
  "(a) If the court finds that all of the estate of the deceased spouse is property passing to the surviving spouse, the court shall issue an order describing the property, determining that the property is property passing to the surviving spouse, and determining that no administration is necessary. The court may issue any further orders which may be necessary to cause delivery of the property or its proceeds to the surviving spouse. (b) If the court finds that all or part of the estate of the deceased spouse is not property passing to the surviving spouse, the court shall issue an order (1) describing any property which is not property passing to the surviving spouse, determining that that property does not pass to the surviving spouse and determining that that property is subject to administration under this code and (2) describing the property, if any, which is property passing to the surviving spouse, determining that that property passes to the surviving spouse, and determining that no administration of that property is necessary. If the court determines that property passes to the surviving spouse, the court may issue any further orders which may be necessary to cause delivery of that property or its proceeds to the surviving spouse. (c) If the petition filed under this chapter includes a description of the interest of the surviving spouse in the community or quasi-community property, or both, which belongs to the surviving spouse pursuant to Section 100 or 101 and the court finds that the interest belongs to the surviving spouse, the court shall issue an order describing the property and confirming the ownership of the surviving spouse and may issue any further orders which may be necessary to cause ownership of the property to be confirmed in the surviving spouse."
  — Cal. Prob. Code § 13656(a)-(c), California Probate Code, the court's orders corresponding to each type of request (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=13656.)

This clause's quotes from § 13656(a) and § 13656(c) are subdivisions of the same section and are not independent confirmations of each other. This document is informational only; it does not itself request or obtain any court order.

WHO MAY FILE, AND IN WHICH COURT
Probate Code § 13650(a) limits who may file this petition to the surviving spouse, or the personal representative, guardian of the estate, or conservator of the estate of the surviving spouse, and fixes venue in the superior court of the county in which the deceased spouse's estate may be administered. Section 13650(c) separately dispenses with any need for a guardian or conservator to obtain authorization from the guardianship or conservatorship court before filing. Two further, separately numbered sections fix which proceeding the petition goes into: Probate Code § 13652 requires that if a proceeding for administration of the deceased spouse's estate is already pending, the petition must be filed in that same proceeding, without payment of an additional filing fee; Probate Code § 13653 provides that if no such proceeding is pending, the petition may, but need not, be filed together with a petition for probate of the will or for administration of the estate.

The petition may also request an order confirming the ownership of the surviving spouse of property belonging to the surviving spouse under Section 100 or 101."
  — Cal. Prob. Code § 13650(a), California Probate Code, standing to file and venue for a spousal or domestic partner property petition (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=13650.)

WHAT THE PETITION MUST ALLEGE AND ATTACH
Probate Code § 13651(a) requires the petition to allege that administration is unnecessary and to set out: if no estate proceeding is pending, the facts needed to determine the proper county of filing; a description of the property alleged to be passing to the surviving spouse, including the trade or business name of any unincorporated business involved; the facts supporting that allegation; a description of any separate community or quasi-community property interest the petitioner asks the court to confirm as already belonging to the surviving spouse under § 100 or § 101; and the name, age, address, and relation to the decedent of each heir and devisee, plus the names and addresses of any named executors and any appointed personal representatives, so far as known — along with disclosure of any written non-pro-rata division agreement between the spouses, or an affirmative statement that none exists. Section 13651(b) requires a copy of the decedent's will to be attached if the petitioner's allegation rests on the will, and § 13651(c) requires a copy of any written non-pro-rata division agreement to be attached if the petitioner's property description rests on one.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-03]
  "A petition filed pursuant to Section 13650 shall allege that administration of all or a part of the estate of the deceased spouse is not necessary for the reason that all or a part of the estate is property passing to the surviving spouse, and shall set forth all of the following information: (1) If proceedings for the administration of the estate are not pending, the facts necessary to determine the county in which the estate of the deceased spouse may be administered. (2) A description of the property of the deceased spouse which the petitioner alleges is property passing to the surviving spouse, including the trade or business name of any property passing to the surviving spouse that consists of an unincorporated business or an interest in an unincorporated business which the deceased spouse was operating or managing at the time of death, subject to any written agreement between the deceased spouse and the surviving spouse providing for a non pro rata division of the aggregate value of the community property assets or quasi-community assets, or both. (3) The facts upon which the petitioner bases the allegation that all or a part of the estate of the deceased spouse is property passing to the surviving spouse. (4) A description of any interest in the community property or quasi-community property, or both, which the petitioner requests the court to confirm to the surviving spouse as belonging to the surviving spouse pursuant to Section 100 or 101, subject to any written agreement between the deceased spouse and the surviving spouse providing for a non pro rata division of the aggregate value of the community property assets or quasi-community assets, or both. (5) The name, age, address, and relation to the deceased spouse of each heir and devisee of the deceased spouse, the names and addresses of all persons named as executors of the will of the deceased spouse, and the names and addresses of all persons appointed as personal representatives of the deceased spouse, which are known to the petitioner. Disclosure of any written agreement between the deceased spouse and the surviving spouse providing for a non pro rata division of the aggregate value of the community property assets or quasi-community property assets, or both, or the affirmative statement that this agreement does not exist."
  — Cal. Prob. Code § 13651(a), California Probate Code, required contents of a spousal or domestic partner property petition (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=13651.)
  "(b) If the petitioner bases the allegation that all or part of the estate of the deceased spouse is property passing to the surviving spouse upon the will of the deceased spouse, a copy of the will shall be attached to the petition. (c) If the petitioner bases the description of the property of the deceased spouse passing to the surviving spouse or the property to be confirmed to the surviving spouse, or both, upon a written agreement between the deceased spouse and the surviving spouse providing for a non pro rata division of the aggregate value of the community property assets or quasi-community assets, or both, a copy of the agreement shall be attached to the petition."
  — Cal. Prob. Code § 13651(b)-(c), California Probate Code, required attachments — the will, and any non-pro-rata division agreement (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=13651.)

NOTICE OF THE HEARING
Probate Code § 13655(a) requires notice of the hearing on the petition — given as provided in Probate Code § 1220 — to each person listed in § 1220, each person named as executor in any will of the deceased spouse, and all devisees and known heirs of the deceased spouse (and, where the petitioner is a trustee of a devisee trust, all persons interested in that trust), whenever an estate proceeding is already pending, or whenever no estate proceeding is pending and the petition is filed on its own rather than together with a petition for probate or administration. Section 13655(b) separately requires that same notice to be delivered to the California Attorney General, addressed to the Attorney General's office in Sacramento, if the petitioner's allegation that property is passing to the surviving spouse rests on the decedent's will and that will involves or may involve a testamentary charitable trust without a resident designated trustee, or a charitable devise without an identified devisee or beneficiary.

(2) All devisees and known heirs of the deceased spouse and, if the petitioner is the trustee of a trust that is a devisee under the will of the decedent, all persons interested in the trust, as determined in cases of future interests pursuant to paragraph (1), (2), or (3) of subdivision (a) of Section 15804."
  — Cal. Prob. Code § 13655(a), California Probate Code, who must receive notice of the petition hearing (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=13655.)

(2) A devise for a charitable purpose without an identified devisee or beneficiary."
  — Cal. Prob. Code § 13655(b), California Probate Code, notice to the Attorney General for petitions involving a charitable interest (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=13655.)

FINALITY OF THE ORDER, AND PROTECTION FOR BUSINESS CREDITORS
Probate Code § 13657 provides that once an order under § 13656 becomes final — whether it determines that property is passing to the surviving spouse or confirms the surviving spouse's ownership of property already belonging to them under § 100 or § 101 — that order 'shall be conclusive on all persons, whether or not they are in being.' Separately, Probate Code § 13658 addresses one specific category of property: if the court determines that property passing to the surviving spouse includes an unincorporated business, or an interest in one, that the decedent was operating or managing at death, the court must require the surviving spouse to file a list of the business's known creditors and the amounts owed to each, and the court may issue any order necessary to protect those creditors' interests, including requiring an undertaking or an inventory and appraisal.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-03]
  "Upon becoming final, an order under Section 13656 (1) determining that property is property passing to the surviving spouse or (2) confirming the ownership of the surviving spouse of property belonging to the surviving spouse under Section 100 or 101 shall be conclusive on all persons, whether or not they are in being."
  — Cal. Prob. Code § 13657, California Probate Code, conclusiveness of a final order under this chapter (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=13657.)
  "If the court determines that all or a part of the property passing to the surviving spouse consists of an unincorporated business or an interest in an unincorporated business which the deceased spouse was operating or managing at the time of death, the court shall require the surviving spouse to file a list of all of the known creditors of the business and the amounts owing to each of them. The court may issue any order necessary to protect the interests of the creditors of the business, including, but not limited to, the filing of (1) an undertaking and (2) an inventory and appraisal in the form provided in Section 8802 and made as provided in Part 3 (commencing with Section 8800) of Division 7."
  — Cal. Prob. Code § 13658, California Probate Code, protection for creditors of an unincorporated business passing to the surviving spouse (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=13658.)

This document is informational only; it does not itself constitute or obtain a final court order.

HOW THIS PETITION DIFFERS FROM THE SMALL ESTATE AFFIDAVIT AND FROM A PETITION FOR PROBATE
This court petition procedure is structurally different from both of this corpus's other estate-administration documents. Unlike the small estate affidavit — a sworn declaration a successor presents directly to a property holder, with no court filing or hearing at all — this petition is filed in superior court, requires notice under Probate Code § 13655, and results in a court order under § 13656 that (per § 13657) becomes conclusive on all persons once final; it produces a recordable judicial determination rather than a private declaration. Unlike a petition for probate, which seeks appointment of a personal representative and, once Letters issue, ongoing court-supervised authority over the whole estate, this petition seeks a one-time determination that administration of specific property is unnecessary or a confirmation of the surviving spouse's existing ownership share — it does not appoint anyone or issue Letters. The procedure is also lighter administratively: Probate Code § 13659 dispenses with the inventory and appraisal that a full probate administration ordinarily requires, except for the unincorporated-business protections of § 13658, and, as already reflected in this corpus's Community Property Agreement — Information Sheet, Probate Code § 13660 lets attorney's fees for this petition be set by private agreement rather than by court approval, with court involvement available only if attorney and client later dispute the fee or its meaning.

However, within three months after the filing of a petition under this chapter, or within such further time as the court or judge for reasonable cause may allow, the petitioner may file with the clerk of the court an inventory and appraisal made as provided in Part 3 (commencing with Section 8800) of Division 7."
  — Cal. Prob. Code § 13659, California Probate Code, no inventory and appraisal ordinarily required for this petition (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=13659.)

  — Cal. Prob. Code § 13660, California Probate Code, attorney's fees for this petition set by private agreement (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=13660.)

(2) A description of the property of the deceased spouse which the petitioner alleges is property passing to the surviving spouse, including the trade or business name of any property passing to the surviving spouse that consists of an unincorporated business or an interest in an unincorporated business which the deceased spouse was operating or managing at the time of death, subject to any written agreement between the deceased spouse and the surviving spouse providing for a non pro rata division of the aggregate value of the community property assets or quasi-community assets, or both. (3) The facts upon which the petitioner bases the allegation that all or a part of the estate of the deceased spouse is property passing to the surviving spouse. (4) A description of any interest in the community property or quasi-community property, or both, which the petitioner requests the court to confirm to the surviving spouse as belonging to the surviving spouse pursuant to Section 100 or 101, subject to any written agreement between the deceased spouse and the surviving spouse providing for a non pro rata division of the aggregate value of the community property assets or quasi-community assets, or both. (5) The name, age, address, and relation to the deceased spouse of each heir and devisee of the deceased spouse, the names and addresses of all persons named as executors of the will of the deceased spouse, and the names and addresses of all persons appointed as personal representatives of the deceased spouse, which are known to the petitioner. Disclosure of any written agreement between the deceased spouse and the surviving spouse providing for a non pro rata division of the aggregate value of the community property assets or quasi-community property assets, or both, or the affirmative statement that this agreement does not exist.

citations.cite: California Probate Code, required attachments — the will, and any non-pro-rata division agreement
citations.quote: (b) If the petitioner bases the allegation that all or part of the estate of the deceased spouse is property passing to the surviving spouse upon the will of the deceased spouse, a copy of the will shall be attached to the petition. (c) If the petitioner bases the description of the property of the deceased spouse passing to the surviving spouse or the property to be confirmed to the surviving spouse, or both, upon a written agreement between the deceased spouse and the surviving spouse providing for a non pro rata division of the aggregate value of the community property assets or quasi-community assets, or both, a copy of the agreement shall be attached to the petition.

expectedJSON.body: Probate Code § 13655(a) requires notice of the hearing on the petition — given as provided in Probate Code § 1220 — to each person listed in § 1220, each person named as executor in any will of the deceased spouse, and all devisees and known heirs of the deceased spouse (and, where the petitioner is a trustee of a devisee trust, all persons interested in that trust), whenever an estate proceeding is already pending, or whenever no estate proceeding is pending and the petition is filed on its own rather than together with a petition for probate or administration. Section 13655(b) separately requires that same notice to be delivered to the California Attorney General, addressed to the Attorney General's office in Sacramento, if the petitioner's allegation that property is passing to the surviving spouse rests on the decedent's will and that will involves or may involve a testamentary charitable trust without a resident designated trustee, or a charitable devise without an identified devisee or beneficiary.

citations.cite: California Probate Code, who must receive notice of the petition hearing
citations.quote: If proceedings for the administration of the estate of the deceased spouse are pending at the time a petition is filed under this chapter, or if the proceedings are not pending and if the petition filed under this chapter is not filed with a petition for probate of the deceased spouse’s will or for administration of the estate of the deceased spouse, notice of the hearing on the petition filed under this chapter shall be given as provided in Section 1220 to all of the following persons: (1) Each person listed in Section 1220 and each person named as executor in any will of the deceased spouse. (2) All devisees and known heirs of the deceased spouse and, if the petitioner is the trustee of a trust that is a devisee under the will of the decedent, all persons interested in the trust, as determined in cases of future interests pursuant to paragraph (1), (2), or (3) of subdivision (a) of Section 15804.

citations.cite: California Probate Code, notice to the Attorney General for petitions involving a charitable interest
citations.quote: The notice specified in subdivision (a) shall also be delivered as provided in subdivision (a) to the Attorney General, addressed to the office of the Attorney General at Sacramento, if the petitioner bases the allegation that all or part of the estate of the deceased spouse is property passing to the surviving spouse upon the will of the deceased spouse and the will involves or may involve either of the following: (1) A testamentary trust of property for charitable purposes other than a charitable trust with a designated trustee, resident in this state. (2) A devise for a charitable purpose without an identified devisee or beneficiary.

expectedJSON.body: Probate Code § 13657 provides that once an order under § 13656 becomes final — whether it determines that property is passing to the surviving spouse or confirms the surviving spouse's ownership of property already belonging to them under § 100 or § 101 — that order 'shall be conclusive on all persons, whether or not they are in being.' Separately, Probate Code § 13658 addresses one specific category of property: if the court determines that property passing to the surviving spouse includes an unincorporated business, or an interest in one, that the decedent was operating or managing at death, the court must require the surviving spouse to file a list of the business's known creditors and the amounts owed to each, and the court may issue any order necessary to protect those creditors' interests, including requiring an undertaking or an inventory and appraisal.

citations.cite: California Probate Code, conclusiveness of a final order under this chapter
citations.quote: Upon becoming final, an order under Section 13656 (1) determining that property is property passing to the surviving spouse or (2) confirming the ownership of the surviving spouse of property belonging to the surviving spouse under Section 100 or 101 shall be conclusive on all persons, whether or not they are in being.

citations.cite: California Probate Code, protection for creditors of an unincorporated business passing to the surviving spouse
citations.quote: If the court determines that all or a part of the property passing to the surviving spouse consists of an unincorporated business or an interest in an unincorporated business which the deceased spouse was operating or managing at the time of death, the court shall require the surviving spouse to file a list of all of the known creditors of the business and the amounts owing to each of them. The court may issue any order necessary to protect the interests of the creditors of the business, including, but not limited to, the filing of (1) an undertaking and (2) an inventory and appraisal in the form provided in Section 8802 and made as provided in Part 3 (commencing with Section 8800) of Division 7.

expectedJSON.body: This court petition procedure is structurally different from both of this corpus's other estate-administration documents. Unlike the small estate affidavit — a sworn declaration a successor presents directly to a property holder, with no court filing or hearing at all — this petition is filed in superior court, requires notice under Probate Code § 13655, and results in a court order under § 13656 that (per § 13657) becomes conclusive on all persons once final; it produces a recordable judicial determination rather than a private declaration. Unlike a petition for probate, which seeks appointment of a personal representative and, once Letters issue, ongoing court-supervised authority over the whole estate, this petition seeks a one-time determination that administration of specific property is unnecessary or a confirmation of the surviving spouse's existing ownership share — it does not appoint anyone or issue Letters. The procedure is also lighter administratively: Probate Code § 13659 dispenses with the inventory and appraisal that a full probate administration ordinarily requires, except for the unincorporated-business protections of § 13658, and, as already reflected in this corpus's Community Property Agreement — Information Sheet, Probate Code § 13660 lets attorney's fees for this petition be set by private agreement rather than by court approval, with court involvement available only if attorney and client later dispute the fee or its meaning.

citations.cite: California Probate Code, no inventory and appraisal ordinarily required for this petition
citations.quote: Except as provided in Section 13658, no inventory and appraisal of the estate of the deceased spouse is required in a proceeding under this chapter. However, within three months after the filing of a petition under this chapter, or within such further time as the court or judge for reasonable cause may allow, the petitioner may file with the clerk of the court an inventory and appraisal made as provided in Part 3 (commencing with Section 8800) of Division 7.

citations.cite: California Probate Code, attorney's fees for this petition set by private agreement
citations.quote: The attorney’s fees for services performed in connection with the filing of a petition and obtaining of a court order under this chapter shall be determined by private agreement between the attorney and the client and are not subject to approval by the court. If there is no agreement between the attorney and the client concerning the attorney’s fees for services performed in connection with the filing of a petition and obtaining of a court order under this chapter and there is a dispute concerning the reasonableness of the attorney’s fees for those services, a petition may be filed with the court in the same proceeding requesting that the court determine the reasonableness of the attorney’s fees for those services.
